authoredPrompt: This figure is an isometric visualization of a single layer's mapping, drawn as two flat square planes stacked one above the other and linked by dashed trajectories. Both planes are outlined in heavy dark gray and carry faint pale gray cross lines through their centers as axis guides. On the lower plane a broad cloud of red dots is scattered over the surface, densest near the middle and thinning toward the corners. Red dashed curves rise from each dot, converging as they climb, and land on the upper plane, where the points no longer fill an area at all: they are packed edge to edge along one short horizontal segment near the plane's back edge, forming a nearly solid red line. Light gray dashed lines trace the frame connecting the corners of the two planes, and a pair of gray arrowheads extends outward along the upper plane in line with the collapsed points. Holding both planes in the same orientation and scale makes the change of shape immediate, as a two-dimensional spread on the input is squeezed onto a one-dimensional locus on the output.
authoredInteractions:
- Animation for the layer mapping; the learner plays the red points rising from the lower plane to the upper plane, the broad 2D cloud collapses into a short line segment, and it becomes clear that the layer reduces spread along one dimension.
- Slider for interpolation through the mapping; the learner scrubs from input to output, dashed trajectories shorten or lengthen and points move continuously, showing how many different inputs can map onto a lower-dimensional locus.
